answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, cut hard from karst, never handed free. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations, each cost blowing through like a zephyr that still has weight. The toll climbs with head count like a comet's lengthening tail, so cheap mass registration stalls against compounding compute.
